title: Jesus Hath Died That I Might Live
description: Jesus Hath Died That I Might Live in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 415.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus hath died that I might live, Might live to God a-lone; In him e-ter-nal life re-ceive, And be in spir-it one.

lines: Jesus hath died that I might live,
Saviour, I thank thee for the grace,
And wait with arms of faith to embrace,
And all thy love to feel.
My soul breaks out in strong desire
My longing heart is all on fire
Give me thyself; from every boast,
Let all I am in thee be lost;
And where thou art is heaven!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
